newsitem.title: USA: DT Industries Q2 backlog up vs year-ago.
newsitem.headline: DT Industries Q2 backlog up vs year-ago.

text.p: DT Industries Inc said Wednesday sales for the second quarter ended December 29 of $100.7 million, up from $60.1 million a year ago, were boosted by recent acquisitions.
Acquisitions also helped its backlog as of December 29 to $173.5 million, or 61.5 percent greater than last year.
"Looking forward, we remain comfortable with internal projections for the remainder of the fiscal year," Stephen Gore, president, said. He did not disclose the projections.
Although the backlog was lower than September 1996 levels, January bookings have been strong and the outlook for future orders is favorable, he added.
Sales in the special machines segment, which includes the DTI Automation and Packaging Groups, increased $40.9 million for the quarter, including $40.1 million from recently acquired businesses.

Sales in the components segment decreased by $300,000 for the quarter, reflecting a reduction in demand for products from customers in the transportation industry that was substantially offset by an increase in sales to several new customers in non-transportation related markets.
"Each of our acquisitions and new technologies has opened the door to further penetrate existing customers, or to expand the breadth of markets we serve," Gore said in a statement.

Earlier, DT, which makes automated production systems, reported second quarter net income of $0.58 a share, up from $0.34 a year ago. The operating margin increased to 13.8 percent from 10.0 percent in the prior year.
"These improvements have resulted not only from the favorable effects of acquisitions, but from production efficiencies, an emphasis on project management and a favorable product mix," Gore said.
